entries.name: Spider Curl
entries.reason: Source-bound side-view draft. The source sets this up its own way, so the drawing follows it and not the usual hanging-arm spider curl: chest and stomach lie against the angled side of a preacher pad, feet on the floor, and the upper arms lie down the pad's other side with their backs resting on it. That far side is drawn sloping, square to the angled side: in this rig a plumb face cannot reach a hanging upper arm, so only the lower part of each upper arm is on the pad. They stay there while the bar is curled from straight arms as far as it goes, held, and lowered slowly to straight arms. Not drawn: the shoulder-width underhand grip, which a side view cannot show; the bar reads end-on at the hands.
entries.summary: Chest and stomach against the angled side of a preacher bench, upper arms on the pad: curl the bar up as far as you can, squeeze, then lower slowly to straight arms.

frames.caption: Lie with the chest and stomach against the angled side of a preacher bench, feet on the floor, upper arms resting on the pad, arms straight.
Keeping the upper arms on the pad, curl the bar up as far as you can.
Lower slowly until the arms are straight.
Chest stays on the bench. Upper arms stay on the pad.
